title: Seat a solar wing on a height-matched tip stay
instruction: In the collar, stand the orange stay whose height matches the top of the yoke block, then seat the blue wing with its root between the rails against the stop and its tip level on the stay.
context: Solar array wings are integrated in 1 g with the free end on a support stand set to the hinge-line height, because the root hinge cannot carry the cantilever and a stand of the wrong height loads it. This tabletop analogue keeps both facts: the stay must go in before the wing, or the wing tips off the yoke, and only the stay as tall as the yoke block leaves the wing level. Tower-building tasks elsewhere force support before span with identical supports. Here the two stays share one colour and diameter and differ only in height, the instruction names no number, and the right one must be matched to the block top by eye, so the wing's final levelness also scores that choice. Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where this job is done; nothing about microgravity is claimed.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up; the table top is the zero of every height below, and the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). Loose parts, rigid and matte: the wing, a dark blue (sRGB 0.10, 0.15, 0.45) slab 220 x 60 x 20 mm, 150 g, lying flat on a 220 x 60 face with its long axis along x, centred at (0.250, 0.350), in the left arm's reach only; the stay, an orange (sRGB 0.95, 0.55, 0.10) cylinder 30 mm in diameter and 50 mm tall, 40 g, standing at (0.220, -0.320), in the right arm's reach only; the short stay, the same orange, 30 mm in diameter and 30 mm tall, 25 g, standing at (0.320, -0.330), in the right arm's reach only. Fixed parts, light grey (sRGB 0.75, 0.75, 0.75), matte: the yoke, just left of the midline, made of the yoke block, 100 x 90 x 50 mm (x, y, z), centred at (0.220, 0.095), spanning x 0.170 to 0.270 and y 0.050 to 0.140, its top 50 mm above the table; on the block two rails 10 x 60 x 40 mm centred at x 0.181 and 0.259, running from y 0.070 to 0.130, their tops 90 mm above the table and their inner faces at x 0.186 and 0.254 (a 68 mm channel, 4 mm per side around the wing); and an end stop 88 x 10 x 40 mm centred at (0.220, 0.135), spanning y 0.130 to 0.140 and joining the rail ends, its stop face at y = 0.130. The collar, a square pocket 40 x 40 mm with walls 7 mm thick and 8 mm tall, centred at (0.220, -0.050): two walls 54 x 7 x 8 mm centred at y -0.0265 and -0.0735 and two walls 7 x 40 x 8 mm centred at x 0.1965 and 0.2435, so the pocket spans x 0.200 to 0.240 and y -0.070 to -0.030 and gives a stay 5 mm of slop per side. Nominal end state: the 50 mm stay upright in the collar, its top 50 mm above the table, level with the block top; the wing along y, its centre at (0.220, 0.016) and 60 mm above the table, its root end face at y = 0.126 (4 mm from the stop) lying on the block between the rails, its tip end at y = -0.094 lying on the stay top and overhanging the stay's far edge by 29 mm. The wing's centre lies between its two supports (the block edge at y = 0.050 and the stay's near edge at y = -0.035), so it rests level; without a stay it tips over the block edge onto the collar's far wall (about 18 degrees), and on the 30 mm stay it tilts about 10 degrees. To build it: print the yoke in PLA as one part (block 100 x 90 x 50 mm with the two rails and the stop on top, 90 mm tall overall) and the collar as one part (54 x 54 x 8 mm with a 40 mm square pocket through it), and tape or screw both to the table at the stated positions; make the wing from foam-core board or a hollow print weighted to 150 g and painted dark blue; print the two stays as solid PLA cylinders (about 40 g and 25 g) and paint them the same orange; tape marks for the three start spots.
scoring: Judged on the end state after both arms have released and withdrawn; in simulation on the final step (SCORE_OVER end) with the stay and the wing at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), so a part still moving or held is not counted. The fixtures cannot move. S: the 50 mm stay stands upright in the collar pocket, its centre within 6 mm of (0.220, -0.050) along x and along y, its bottom within 3 mm of the table and its axis within 5 degrees of vertical; the 30 mm stay never counts. The wing is measured at the midpoint of the bottom edge of each end face (the edge on the face that points down, so either broad face may be up); the root end is the end nearer the stop. W, the root is captured: the wing lies on a broad face (its 60 mm width within 10 degrees of horizontal and its 220 mm length within 25 degrees of horizontal; a seated wing is level, a tipped one about 18 degrees, one stood on its end near 90), and the root end's bottom edge is within 5 mm of the channel centreline x = 0.220, 0 to 10 mm short of the stop face (y 0.120 to 0.130, with up to 2 mm into the stop allowed for solver penetration) and at most 85 mm above the table (a seated root is at 50 mm, a tipped one about 74 mm, the rail tops at 90 mm). L, the wing is level on both supports: W, both end bottom edges 46 to 54 mm above the table (a tilt under about 2 degrees), and the tip end within 10 mm of x = 0.220. Score, gated on S because the support must go in first: S and L, 1.0, the success condition, which ends the trial once it has held for 1 s. S and W without L, 0.5: both parts placed but the wing skewed in the channel with its tip end more than 10 mm off the centreline, or high or low by more than 4 mm at an end, for example resting on the 30 mm stay stacked on the 50 mm one. S alone, 0.25: the stay set with no wing captured, for example the wing still on its mark, across the rail tops, flat on the table, on its edge, stood on its end, or more than 10 mm from the stop. No S, 0, whatever the wing does: a wing seated with no stay tips onto the collar, and on the 30 mm stay it tilts, and both are the failures this task tests. A wing level on the 50 mm stay standing outside the collar, or 7 mm off its centre, scores 0 too. Every outcome falls in exactly one tier. A value exactly on a limit passes, and lengths carry a 0.1 mm margin. A tape measure checks the heights and the 3, 5, 6 and 10 mm offsets. A top photo shows whether the root sits between the rails; the stay left on its start mark, or a side photo, shows which stay is in the collar. In simulation every horizontal and orientation test uses the parts' centres and quaternions, not their axis-aligned bounds, and the scorer cannot see the grippers, so a part held perfectly still in a passing pose reads as placed; on the real rig the photo after the arms withdraw decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the wing back flat on its mark with its long axis forward and stand both stays back on their marks; the yoke and the collar do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours; the yoke, rails, stop and collar are static colliders that cannot move. A real wing root is bolted to a hinge and the stand is adjustable; here the root sits by gravity in a rail channel with 4 mm of side clearance and the stand is one of two loose dowels keyed by a collar, so choosing the right dowel replaces the adjustment. The wing is a solid 20 mm slab at 150 g, not a honeycomb panel, and its deflection is not modelled. Earth gravity on a bench, by construction; nothing about microgravity is claimed.
